decon throughput, waste handling, clothing/property replacement, follow-up instructions, and medical referral are planned and exercised

reentry/relocation decisions have criteria, authority, maps, dose/contamination evidence, appeal, and plain-language notices
food, water, milk, livestock, farms, fish/game, and drinking-water controls include replacement benefits and small-business/farm continuity
cleanup, waste staging/disposal, property records, worker protection, and public involvement are planned before late-phase decisions
claims intake connects evacuation costs, housing, wages, medical records, farm losses, school disruption, property, and documentation replacement
school continuity, childcare, long-term care, disability services, dialysis/oxygen, chronic care, pets/livestock, and displaced-worker supports are not left for improvisation
residents and local institutions can challenge maps, inaccessible alerts, denied claims, bad sampling, or missing recovery support, with closure evidence
behavioral health, risk communication, stigma prevention, community monitoring access, and trusted messengers are treated as recovery infrastructure
